oldArch.title: Ancient Indian Architecture
oldArch.function: Traditional Indian architecture is rooted in Sacred Geometry (Vastu Shastra), rock-cut sanctuaries, and monumental temple superstructures (Shikhara and Vimana).
facts: Vastu Shastra provides astronomical alignment and principles of spatial geometry.
Kailasa Temple at Ellora was carved out of a single monolithic rock from the top down.
Intricate passive cooling and natural ventilation techniques were engineered into ancient palaces and stepwells (Baolis).

modernArch.title: Modern Indian Architecture
modernArch.function: Contemporary Indian architecture synthesizes ancient climate-responsive principles with modern structural materials, parametric shapes, and sustainable design.
facts: Combines traditional jali (lattice) screens for solar shading with modern glass & steel.
Emphasizes eco-friendly materials, rainwater harvesting, and zero-carbon building design.
Iconic examples include the Lotus Temple in New Delhi and modern eco-friendly campuses.
